key_patterns.name: Multiplex network with heterogeneous tie strength
key_patterns.description: Contacts are organized in family, work_school, and community layers; family ties are fewer but stronger and more frequent, community ties are more numerous but weaker.
key_patterns.relevance: Layer-specific influence weights should reflect differential exposure and conformity pressure, affecting adoption speed and clustering.

key_patterns.name: Demographic and occupational homophily
key_patterns.description: Edges are more likely within the same age_group and occupation (especially within work_school).
key_patterns.relevance: Homophily shapes diffusion paths, increases assortativity of adoption, and can produce persistent group adoption gaps.

key_patterns.name: Skewed risk_perception
key_patterns.description: risk_perception is bounded [0,1] and typically right- or left-skewed depending on population; expect age/occupation gradients (e.g., older or healthcare-related roles higher).
key_patterns.relevance: Baseline propensity to adopt masks varies by agent; calibrating its distribution and group differences is key to initial adoption and heterogeneous responses.

key_patterns.name: S-shaped adoption trajectory
key_patterns.description: Panel wearing_mask over days generally follows slow start, rapid growth, then plateau.
key_patterns.relevance: Supports use of threshold or logistic influence models; helps define diffusion_speed and time_to_threshold targets.

key_patterns.name: Information precedes adoption
key_patterns.description: received_info at t-1 strongly predicts wearing_mask at t, controlling for prior state.
key_patterns.relevance: Calibration should include an information diffusion sub-process that feeds adoption hazard.

key_patterns.name: Peer influence and clustering
key_patterns.description: Higher peer_mask_rate among neighbors increases adoption probability; adoption states cluster on the network (positive assortativity).
key_patterns.relevance: Set and calibrate social influence coefficients and layer weights; evaluate assortativity_of_adoption.

key_patterns.name: Early adopters are higher risk and/or central
key_patterns.description: Agents with higher risk_perception and higher degree/centrality tend to adopt earlier.
key_patterns.relevance: Prioritize seeding and susceptibility parameterization; use to estimate behavioral_R0 in the early phase.

key_patterns.name: Non-negligible de-adoption
key_patterns.description: Transitions from wearing_mask=1 to 0 occur when peer norms weaken or info fades.
key_patterns.relevance: Include a small abandonment probability to match steady_state_adoption and late-phase dynamics.

key_distributions.name: Layer-specific degree distributions
key_distributions.description: Degree per agent differs by layer; family is low-variance/low-mean, work_school moderate, community overdispersed.
key_distributions.parameters: For each layer L in {family, work_school, community}, fit Negative Binomial with mean μ_L and dispersion k_L (or Poisson if k_L -> ∞).

key_distributions.name: Risk perception
key_distributions.description: Bounded continuous propensity in [0,1], often skewed.
key_distributions.parameters: Beta(a, b); estimate (a, b) overall and by age_group/occupation strata.

key_distributions.name: Time-to-adoption (first adoption)
key_distributions.description: Survival time from day 0 to first wearing_mask=1, conditional on exposures.
key_distributions.parameters: Weibull(shape k, scale λ) or Log-logistic; estimate separately for groups and early vs growth phases.

key_distributions.name: Exposures to adoption
key_distributions.description: Number of mask-wearing neighbor-exposure days before adoption.
key_distributions.parameters: Negative Binomial with mean m_exp and dispersion r_exp; also compute median exposures.

key_distributions.name: Information arrival hazard
key_distributions.description: Probability per day of received_info=1 given neighbor info/adoption by layer.
key_distributions.parameters: Per-layer transmission probabilities p_info_L and exogenous broadcast rate p_info_exo.

key_distributions.name: Abandonment (de-adoption)
key_distributions.description: Daily probability of switching from wearing_mask=1 to 0.
key_distributions.parameters: Bernoulli with probability p_off; allow dependence on peer_mask_rate.

key_relationships.relationship: Positive effect; information exposure increases next-day adoption odds.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate odds ratio via discrete-time logistic regression; typically OR > 1.5 (to be fit on panel).

key_relationships.relationship: Monotone positive; diminishing returns possible at high prevalence.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate coefficient β and potential nonlinearity (e.g., quadratic term); medium to strong.

key_relationships.relationship: Higher risk_perception increases baseline hazard independent of peers.
key_relationships.strength: Estimate coefficient α; moderate strength; heterogeneity across groups.

key_relationships.relationship: Systematic differences in timing and final adoption levels by group.
key_relationships.strength: Quantify via group fixed effects and compute group_adoption_gap; moderate.

key_relationships.relationship: More central agents adopt earlier and trigger more downstream adoptions.
key_relationships.strength: Compute correlation and early-phase behavioral_R0; moderate.

key_relationships.relationship: Family ties exert stronger influence than work_school, which is stronger than community.
key_relationships.strength: Infer relative weights w_family > w_work_school > w_community; strong qualitative ordering.

layer_weights.notes: Calibrate these via maximizing fit to exposures_to_adoption and diffusion_speed; enforce sum to 1.

symmetrize_edges.source: Multiplex network JSON (note: reciprocity not guaranteed)
symmetrize_edges.notes: Treat influence as undirected unless directionality is known; deduplicate edges.

degree_means_by_layer.notes: Compute μ_L = mean degree per layer L; also fit dispersion k_L for Negative Binomial.

assortativity_targets.source: Multiplex network JSON (homophily); typical workplace homophily
assortativity_targets.notes: Replace with empirical assortativity coefficients; use as validation targets.

adoption_function.value: p(adopt)_i,t = sigmoid(α*risk_i + β*Σ_L w_L*peer_mask_rate_{i,L,t-1} + δ*received_info_{i,t-1} + γ*policy_t + η_group[i] - θ)
adoption_function.notes: Synchronous daily updates; compute peer rates excluding ego; η_group is group fixed effect; θ is intercept/threshold.

alpha_risk_weight.source: Panel regression on wearing_mask_t ~ risk_perception + controls (recommended default if not yet fit)
alpha_risk_weight.notes: Estimate via discrete-time logistic regression; expect 1.0–3.0; adjust to match early adoption gradient by risk.

beta_peer_influence.notes: Strong social norm effect typical; calibrate to match diffusion_speed and behavioral_R0.

delta_info_effect.notes: Set by the strength of information campaigns; tune to match exposures_to_adoption and early lift.

gamma_policy_effect.notes: If no explicit policy time series, keep γ active but policy_t=0; otherwise fit to observed jumps.

theta_intercept.notes: Controls baseline propensity; set to match initial adoption_rate.

nonlinearity_peer_quadratic.source: Check diminishing returns at high peer prevalence
nonlinearity_peer_quadratic.notes: Optional quadratic term on peer rate; include if improves fit (likelihood/BIC).

abandonment_prob_per_day.notes: Allow p_off to depend on peer_mask_rate (decrease with higher peer rate).

stubborn_fraction.source: Panel censoring: never-adopters by end of window despite exposures
stubborn_fraction.notes: Agents with capped max adoption probability or infinite threshold.

compliance_ceiling.notes: Upper bound on individual adoption probability to prevent unrealistic 100% adoption without policy.

info_transmission_per_layer.notes: Probability per day that an informed neighbor causes received_info=1; calibrate via hazard models.

exogenous_broadcast_rate.notes: Represents media/policy broadcasts; can be time-varying if policy schedule known.

info_decay_prob.notes: Probability per day that info salience decays; if received_info is absorbing in data, set to 0.

initial_adoption_rate.source: Panel wearing_mask on day 0 (default if not available)
initial_adoption_rate.notes: Set per agent as Bernoulli with p = sigmoid(α*risk + η_group - θ0); θ0 tuned to match day-0 mean.

initial_information_rate.source: Panel received_info on day 0 (default if not available)
initial_information_rate.notes: Seed info heterogeneously across groups per observed rates.

seeding_strategy.source: Early adopters often central; improves match to early behavioral_R0
seeding_strategy.notes: If panel identifies early adopters, seed accordingly; else seed by high risk_perception and centrality.

adoption_target.notes: Used for time_to_threshold and diffusion_speed; set to observed steady_state if available.

observation_window.notes: Compute steady_state_adoption as mean over the last observation_window days.

group_susceptibility_multipliers.source: Panel group differences in hazard; attributes CSV
group_susceptibility_multipliers.notes: Multiply α for each group; fit from group fixed effects.

occupation_influence_scalers.notes: Scales β for work_school layer by occupation context.

num_replicates.notes: Compute confidence intervals of evaluation metrics across runs.

random_seed.notes: Settable per experiment; vary across replicates if needed.

preprocessing_steps.step: Load agent_attributes.csv and encode age_group and occupation as categorical integers; validate risk_perception in [0,1].
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Prepare static agent heterogeneity and ensure valid ranges.

preprocessing_steps.step: Load multiplex network JSON; cast keys to ints; deduplicate and symmetrize edges per layer; remove self-loops.
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Construct clean layer-specific adjacency for influence calculations.

preprocessing_steps.step: Join panel (day, agent_id, wearing_mask, received_info) with agent attributes; ensure day 0 exists and sort by (agent_id, day).
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Create longitudinal dataset with covariates and states.

preprocessing_steps.step: Compute peer_mask_rate_{i,L,t-1} for each agent, layer, and day using neighbors’ wearing_mask at t-1; aggregate Σ_L w_L*peer rates.
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Build social exposure variables for hazard modeling.

preprocessing_steps.step: Derive adoption events (0->1) and de-adoption events (1->0); compute time-to-adoption and exposures-to-adoption per agent.
Compute network and behavioral metrics over time: adoption_rate, assortativity_of_adoption (by state), group_adoption_gap (by age_group/occupation).
preprocessing_steps.purpose: Establish empirical targets for simulation validation.

preprocessing_steps.step: Partition timeline into early (<10% adoption), growth (10%–adoption_target), and late (post adoption_target).

calibration_strategy.calibration_approach: 1) Estimate a discrete-time logistic hazard model for adoption: Pr(adopt_t=1 | not yet adopted) = logit^{-1}(θ + α*risk + β*Σ_L w_L*peer_mask_rate_{L,t-1} + δ*received_info_{t-1} + η_group + ε). Fit with agent-clustered SEs; optionally add quadratic term for peer rate and random effects. 2) Estimate information transmission: For each layer, fit received_info_t ~ Σ_L q_L*peer_info_{L,t-1} + exogenous rate; map q_L to p_info_L. 3) Estimate abandonment probability p_off via logistic regression of de-adoption on peer rate and time. 4) Identify stubborn_fraction as proportion of agents never adopting despite exceeding exposure threshold (e.g., >k exposure-days). 5) Use the fitted coefficients as priors; then run simulation and apply Bayesian optimization or Approximate Bayesian Computation to jointly tune {β, w_L, δ, θ, p_info_L, p_off, stubborn_fraction} to minimize a weighted loss over targets: RMSE(adoption_rate_t), |time_to_threshold - observed|, |steady_state_adoption - observed|, |diffusion_speed - observed|, |assortativity_of_adoption - observed|, |group_adoption_gap - observed|, |behavioral_R0 - observed|, |exposures_to_adoption - observed|.
calibration_strategy.validation_strategy: Hold out the last T_holdout days (e.g., final 20%) and a random 10% subgraph (or community) for out-of-sample validation. For each calibrated parameter set, run N replicates and compute prediction intervals for adoption_rate, time_to_threshold, steady_state_adoption, diffusion_speed, assortativity, group_adoption_gap. Perform posterior predictive checks on: (a) distribution of time-to-adoption and exposures-to-adoption (K-S tests), (b) early-phase behavioral_R0 estimated via causal timing attribution (who adopted after direct neighbor adoption within lag window), (c) stability under policy counterfactuals if available. Conduct sensitivity analysis (one-at-a-time and global, e.g., Sobol) for α, β, w_L, p_info_L, p_off to assess robustness.

file_summaries:
Semantic metadata summary for agent_attributes.csv

- Data structure/type: Flat, tabular CSV. One row per agent; no nesting. Suitable for direct DataFrame loading.
- Primary key: agent_id (integer, unique per agent). Must align with node IDs in the social network graph.
- Columns and meanings:
  - agent_id: Unique agent identifier used for cross-file joins and simulation indexing.
  - age_group: Categorical demographic stratum (e.g., Youth, Young Adult, Middle Age; possibly others). Used for demographic heterogeneity and homophily.
  - occupation: Categorical role/context (e.g., Student, White Collar, Blue Collar). Maps agents to context-specific contact layers (school, office, workplace) and schedules.
  - risk_perception: Continuous float in [0,1], representing each agent’s perceived health risk. Interpretable as baseline propensity to adopt mask-wearing absent social influence or policy pressure.
- Relationships/nesting: None within the file. Expected external relationships:
  - One-to-one with nodes in a social network (edges file).
  - Many-to-one grouping by age_group or occupation for layer-specific mixing and interventions.
- Intended use in simulation:
  - Initialization of agent attributes (static): age_group, occupation, risk_perception.
  - Initialization of agent state (dynamic, not in file): mask_wearing_status, which should be derived from risk_perception and early conditions.
  - Behavior update rules: risk_perception informs baseline adoption threshold; combine with peer mask prevalence from the network and exogenous factors (e.g., policy) via a function such as p(adopt) = sigmoid(α*risk_perception + β*peer_mask_rate + γ*policy + …).
  - Network dynamics: age_group and occupation drive homophily, contact rates, and layer membership (household, school, workplace, community).
  - Heterogeneity: use categories to parameterize differing influence susceptibility, compliance ceilings, or exposure to targeted campaigns.
- Data types/validation:
  - agent_id: int, unique, no gaps required but consistency with graph IDs is critical.
  - age_group/occupation: categorical strings; define controlled vocab to avoid typos.
  - risk_perception: float [0,1]; clip/validate if out-of-range; consider imputation strategy if missing.
- Simulation design implications:
  - Supports multi-layer network modeling (occupation-based layers).
  - Enables demographic stratification of adoption dynamics and policy effects.
  - Provides seed for initial mask adoption distribution (e.g., probabilistic draw by risk_perception).
- Performance/encoding notes:
  - Encode categorical fields to integers for efficiency.
  - Store mapping dictionaries for reproducibility across runs.
- Limitations:
  - No direct network structure or household membership included; requires external edge/context data.
  - No explicit health status or policy exposure fields; must be modeled or sourced elsewhere.

- Overall structure and type
  - JSON object representing a multiplex (multi-layer) social network.
  - Top-level keys are stringified node IDs; values are objects with arrays of neighbor IDs by relationship layer.
  - Static, unweighted edges; no timestamps or attributes.

- Meaning of keys
  - Top-level keys (e.g., "0", "1", "2"): unique agent identifiers (cast to int when loading).
  - Nested keys:
    - family: household/kin contacts
    - work_school: colleagues/classmates
    - community: broader community ties (friends, neighbors, casual contacts)
  - Array values: integer IDs of other agents connected in that layer.

- Relationships and nested elements
  - Each agent maps to three lists of alters; each list defines edges within a distinct layer.
  - Layers are disjoint categories but the same alter may appear in multiple layers (multi-relational tie).
  - Reciprocity is not guaranteed; edges may be directed in the data even if intended as undirected. Consider symmetrizing if needed.
  - Some alters may exist as neighbors without their own entry; handle by creating nodes with empty lists if absent.
  - Potential duplicates within a list should be de-duplicated on load.

- How this informs simulation entities and interactions
  - Agents: one per ID; maintain state variables (e.g., mask_wearing, susceptibility, conformity, stubbornness).
  - Network: build three adjacency structures (family, work_school, community) and optionally an aggregate with layer tags.
  - Interaction dynamics:
    - Apply layer-specific contact frequencies and influence weights (e.g., family > work_school > community).
    - Compute adoption pressure per agent by aggregating neighbors’ states per layer, with normalization by degree.
    - Support multiplex effects when the same alter appears in multiple layers (sum or otherwise combine weights).
    - Decide on directed vs undirected influence; if symmetrized, add missing reciprocal edges.
  - Initialization and scheduling:
    - Convert keys to ints; generate node set as union of all keys and neighbor IDs.
    - Assign baseline adoption, seed nodes, and heterogeneity parameters.
    - Run discrete time steps with layer-weighted updates; optionally stochastic adoption and decay/abandonment.
  - Validation/consistency checks:
    - Ensure no self-loops unless intended; handle missing nodes; confirm max ID (sample suggests up to 99).

- Data structure and type: Flat, tabular CSV; a longitudinal (panel) dataset with one record per agent per day. Boolean fields likely encoded as true/false strings.
- Columns/keys meaning:
  - day: Discrete timestep (integer, day-level granularity).
  - agent_id: Unique agent identifier; repeats across days.
  - wearing_mask: Agent’s behavioral state at that day (binary).
  - received_info: Whether the agent had received mask-related information by/on that day (binary).
- Relationships/nested elements:
  - No nesting; purely flat.
  - Repeated measures over time for each agent_id form trajectories.
  - Temporal dependency implied: wearing_mask at day t may depend on previous days and on received_info.
  - Network structure is not included; any social ties must come from another source.
- How this informs simulation:
  - Agent initialization: Create agents by agent_id; set initial states from day 0 (mask-wearing and information exposure).
  - State variables: Each agent maintains two core states—information exposure and mask-wearing.
  - Transition modeling: Use sequences to estimate/calibrate probabilities/hazard of adopting masks conditional on received_info (e.g., P(mask_t=1 | info_t-1), baseline adoption without info).
  - Information dynamics: received_info can be treated as an exogenous label in training; in simulation, it should be endogenized via the social network (neighbors’ influence, broadcast campaigns).
  - Update scheme: Synchronous daily updates consistent with the day timestep in the data.
  - Validation: Compare simulated adoption curves over days against aggregated wearing_mask rates in this dataset.
